subject: [PATCH for-7.4 0/9] memcg: remove the v1 soft limit

reviews.author: T.J. Mercier
reviews.summary: Reviewer T.J. Mercier noted that the removal of the soft limit rbtree would leave MEMCG_LRU_HEAD unreachable and suggested removing it along with the corresponding operation.
sentiment_signals: reviewer's comment was neutral, but provided a suggestion
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Aug 13, 2026 at 1:27 AM Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com> wrote:
>
> On Tue 11-08-26 13:32:00, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> > The soft limit rbtree was the only caller. Dropping it leaves
> > MEMCG_LRU_HEAD unreachable, since nothing else ever rotates a memcg with
> > that op, so remove the op too and update the memcg LRU comment.
> >
> > Signed-off-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>
>
> I am not deeply familiar with MGLRU to give my ack but from a quick look
> this looks right.

This looks good to me.

Reviewed-by: T.J. Mercier <tjmercier@google.com>

2026-08-19.patch_summary: This patch removes the v1 soft limit feature from the Linux kernel's memory cgroup (memcg) implementation, which was deprecated in version 6.12 and has been replaced by v2 features such as memory.low and memory.min. The removal includes changes to various files, including memcontrol-v1.c, mm/vmscan.c, and include/linux/memcontrol.h, where the soft limit reclaim functionality is removed and related code is simplified or deleted.
